description: Redo AI product photo and video examples from your own photo: a desk photo, or a short ad with an actor, voice, and captions. Credits (plan units) show first.
h1: See It. Recreate It. AI Product Photo and Video Examples
lead: Start from a photo you would actually run, and get your own version with the product you sell. The desk card already picked the room and the crop. Drop your item into that frame, and the same quiet setting comes back as your file. A short ad from that still is a separate file.
card: Six product photos you can recreate, from a travel mug to a sunscreen tube, plus a way to start a short ad.
intro: You can see the size and the setting before you spend a credit. The tote card puts the bag beside clothes so a shopper can judge the size. Use your own tote in that frame, and turn the still into a short ad when you want motion.
steps_h2: How to Recreate an Example in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You get your own version of a scene you would actually post. Pick the card, add the item you sell, and take the file.

steps.d: Look at the room and the crop. Open the card that already looks like the post you would run for this product.
One photo of the whole product is enough. A product page works when its pictures are of the item you ship.
Check the product against the item you ship, then save the photo or publish the short ad.

faq.q: What is an example on this page?
faq.a: It is a photo with the setting already chosen, not an empty prompt box. One card is a desk and a crop. You bring the item you sell. A short ad is a later choice, after that still looks like the item in your box.

faq.q: How does an example become my file?
faq.a: Paste the product page or upload one photo, then type the one sentence the ad should say. For a serum, the bottle photo is enough. A photo costs 24 credits, and a 15-second video costs 60. The cost shows before anything runs.

faq.q: Why start here instead of booking a creator?
faq.a: You can try a second opening without waiting on a creator's calendar. A shop selling phone grips can drop yesterday's photo into a desk scene this afternoon, then make another file that opens on a different line. Each file is its own credit charge, and you pick which one to post.

faq.q: Which shops get the most from these examples?
faq.a: A one-person shop packing orders at night gets the most from these cards. A marketer who has to hand a client a file by Friday, and a founder who has never booked a studio, use them the same way. A brand that already photographs every product in-house can skip this page.

faq.q: Can I use an example if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. Taking a photo of the whole item and opening a card is the skill this page asks for. You type one sentence, and the spoken line is filled in from that. There is no timeline to learn.
Small packages and larger ones both fit these scenes. A tea tin uses the same cards: pick the crop that fits a small package, then compare the tin in the file with the tin you ship.

faq.q: Can the product come from a photo I took?
faq.a: Yes. The item in the file comes from the photo you upload, or from a product page you paste. Show the whole product. See [URL to video](page:url-to-video).

faq.q: Where can I post the file?
faq.a: Most shops post the tall 9:16 file first, because it fills a phone. Use 1:1 when the placement is a square feed, and 16:9 when the placement is YouTube. 4:3 and 3:4 are there when a slot asks for them. You can publish from here, or download the file and put it on your store.

faq.q: Do I pay to make a file from an example?
faq.a: Yes. The pictures on this page only show the look. A file you make spends credits on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark, so it can run as a paid placement and sit on your product page. A file you make for a client is the same kind of download. You still follow the ad account's rules on what the video is allowed to claim.

faq.q: Why not build the ad from a blank page?
faq.a: A blank page makes you invent the desk, the crop, and the first line at the same time. The desk card already chose the room. You only decide whether the item in the photo is yours, and what the voice should say.
